transcript:
Header: 2026-07-08 14:30 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Anna (Elysian Head of Trust), Liam (CTO), Priya (Infra), Jonas (Legal)

Summary: Quick security/compliance alignment. Primary ask: ensure EU-only processing for EU customer data, map KMS options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), confirm subprocessor footprint and contractual guarantees, discuss audit logs/retention, and next steps for a short EU-limited pilot.

Topics: data residency, region pinning, KMS customer-managed vs escrow, audit logs retention, SSO/SAML and RBAC, subprocessor transparency, SOC2/ISO evidence

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're on the 14:30 slot, I see folks on the call, can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Anna: Hi I'm Anna, head of trust at Elysian, I run our security program, glad to be here.
[00:12] Liam: Liam, CTO, focus on infra and legal ops.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, infra, I'll be doing the KMS work.
[00:18] Jonas: Jonas from legal, I'll handle DPA/SCC questions.
[00:22] Carlos: Carlos, solutions engineer, Redwood.
[00:24] Maya: Cool. High level: Elysian's ask was around EU-only processing for EU customers, and KMS mapping — options for customer-managed keys, plus auditing and subprocessors. We'll be concise then go deeper.
[00:36] Anna: Yes, main constraint is we cannot have EU customer PII leave EU borders per our contracts. We also need 7 year log retention for certain events and per-user RBAC.
[00:47] Liam: Also curious about what parts of inference touch US-based subprocessors — we saw a S3-like mention in your docs and want clarification.
[00:55] Maya: Absolutely. Quick framing: Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated pools, and private deployments. For EU-only processing we can do region pinning inside the hosted plane or run a private deployment in your VPC. For pilot, hosted with EU routing is usually fastest.
[01:10] Priya: When you say region pinning, is it strict? If a pod in EU goes down, will calls fail over to US? That's a hard no for us.
[01:19] Carlos: Good question. By default our smart routing will prefer same-region capacity; we can enforce strict affinity as a policy — which disallows cross-region fallback. Enabling strict affinity is an SLO tradeoff (possible increased error rate under outages) but satisfies residency. We also offer canary/fallback policies that are configurable.
[01:33] Jonas: And contractual guarantees — is strict affinity covered by SLA language? We need to be able to put that in the DPA.
[01:38] Maya: We can propose region-pinning addendum language. For pilots we typically document routing policy and provide operational playbooks; for enterprise contracts we can include language binding routing to EU-only endpoints.
[01:48] Anna: Great. KMS — options? Customer-managed keys in our KMS vs Redwood-managed keys.
[01:54] Carlos: Two main options: 1) Customer-managed keys (CMK) where you bring your KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS) and we call out to your key for envelope encryption; we support AES-256 at rest and in-transit TLS 1.3. 2) Redwood-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS — faster onboarding but keys live in Redwood's control. Both support BYOK semantics, but CMK implies additional operational steps (rotation, IAM).
[02:15] Priya: If we do CMK and key material stays in EU region, does any metadata or key gradient leave EU during tokenization or cache operations? Also, what about KV cache?
[02:26] Carlos: The KV cache is stored in the serving region for low-latency. We will ensure caches for EU-pinned workloads reside in EU hosts. For CMK we never export raw key material; we only call the KMS in-region for decrypt/encrypt operations. There are subtle things: if you use cross-region KMS replicas, you'd need to confirm they stay in EU.
[02:43] Liam: Any subprocessors that are US-based that might touch telemetry or logs?
[02:49] Maya: We maintain a subprocessor inventory; primary infra providers in EU (cloud regions) plus some analytics and monitoring vendors that may be US-based. We can provide a redacted list initially and full list under NDA.
[02:59] Anna: Redacted list is okay for now but we'll need the full list for our privacy team.
[03:03] Maya: Understood, we'll attach that.
[03:06] Jonas: On the legal side, transfers — do you rely on SCCs or any EU adequacy?
[03:11] Maya: We primarily rely on SCCs where applicable; where customers require, we can support additional contractual addenda and discuss supplementary measures (encryption at rest/in-transit, minimized logs, contractual restrictions on subprocessors).
[03:22] Anna: About logs: we need audit logs for admin activity, token-level access and model execution traces for 7 years for a subset of accounts. Can Redwood retain logs that long and provide exports on request?
[03:35] Carlos: Yes, logs retention is configurable. For hosted we can provision longer retention buckets but retention costs apply. We can export logs in parquet/JSON and push to your S3 in EU or deliver via secure transfer. A note: some debug-level traces may include query text; that can be redacted or hashed before retention per your policy.
[03:54] Priya: Hashing query text is okay for telemetry, but for auditing we sometimes need original strings for specific cases. How do we handle privileges?
[04:03] Carlos: RBAC + SSO integration will control who can request unredacted logs. We support SAML2.0/Okta/IdP federation and fine-grained roles: read-only, log-admin, key-admin. Key-admin would be the only role able to request rehydration of encrypted logs if you choose to keep encrypted-at-rest content.
[04:20] Liam: Is there a separation of duty where Redwood ops cannot decrypt customer logs?
[04:25] Carlos: With CMK and key policy that denies Redwood principal from Decrypt, we can ensure that Redwood does not have the cryptographic ability to decrypt. That requires your KMS policy to explicitly exclude our service role. It also affects supportability: if Redwood can't decrypt, some debugging for incidents will need to be done with you providing temporary decryption or reproducer data.
[04:45] Anna: That's acceptable; we prefer security over convenience.
[04:48] Jonas: What about SOC2 and ISO attestation evidence? Can you share penetration test summaries and SOC2 Type II report?
[04:55] Maya: Yes, we will share our SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate through a secure portal; we also have a red-team summary and pen test executive summary. We'll redact customer-specific data.
[05:05] Anna: Please include evidence of control for key management and subprocessor oversight.
[05:09] Maya: Sure.
[05:11] Priya: For the EU-only pilot, what does onboarding look like? We need a small proof where all EU tenant traffic stays in EU and logs get pushed to our EU S3 and keys are in our EU KMS.
[05:23] Carlos: Typical approach: 1) provision EU-only routing policy and strict affinity for that tenant, 2) configure CMK with key policy that restricts Redwood key operations as discussed, 3) set up log forwarder to your EU S3 bucket, 4) run test corpus and latency checks. We can do that in 5-7 business days if approvals move quickly.
[05:40] Liam: Are there known feature limitations when region-pinning is strict — for example, model variants or auto-fallback?
[05:48] Carlos: Yes: strict affinity can prevent cross-region burst capacity, so if your traffic spikes beyond EU capacity you may see throttling or errors. Also some models are only available on certain hardware families; we can provision dedicated capacity for the pilot to ensure parity. We will surface those tradeoffs in the runbook.
[06:04] Anna: About subprocessors doing ML model training or serving — do you have any split where model artifacts are trained in the US but served in EU?
[06:13] Maya: We separate model training and serving. Training pipelines may touch global infra, but for inference we can ensure model weights used in EU-serving are stored and loaded from EU storage. If customers need training isolation, that's part of Private deployment discussions.
[06:27] Jonas: SCCs are fine but we may require supplementary measures; will Redwood support minimized logs and cryptographic controls as extra contractual measures?
[06:36] Maya: Yes, we can include technical and contractual supplementary measures. We'll surface options in the DPA redline.
[06:42] Priya: On KMS integration, do you have sample terraform modules or Kubernetes operators? We prefer IaC.
[06:49] Carlos: Yes, we'll share a terraform module and a short Helm chart snippet for the sidecar that talks to KMS. I will send the repo link in the follow-up. Note that some customers integrate via VPC peering and a private endpoint for KMS to keep traffic internal.
[07:03] Liam: Regarding auditability, are there immutable event logs with sequence numbers for model invocations? We need tamper-evidence.
[07:11] Carlos: We persist event streams with append-only semantics and cryptographic checksums; we also support exporting digest manifests to your S3 for independent verification.
